checks: A triangulation of the selected support with exactly its vertices can be formed by pulling and stellar insertion, including degenerate rank zero separately. Its graph is connected, with at least N−1 edges.

Each edge midpoint is integral by parity, lies in an actual fiber by convexity, and lies in an edge relative interior, so is distinct from every selected vertex and every other edge midpoint. Thus M≥2N−1.

The nonnegative deficit is an integer. At least two affine dimensions give a full simplex with a triangular cycle, so the connected graph would have at least N edges and the deficit would be at least one. The ≤1/4 premise excludes this.

Rank zero gives N=M=1. In rank one the primitive difference and endpoint parity give 2L intervening steps. The lifted segment supplies all even sites of the same selected class and all odd sites, so N=L+1. Equality exhausts the trace, and singleton fibers force the segment's affine heights.

Each pair opposite the middle point has nonnegative affine margin on at least one member of any containing closed halfspace. Including the middle gives N/(2N−1)>1/2, also valid for the singleton case.
Original 25aee623d8e5a8b7 §6 gives the same counting specialization. The independent graph-cycle argument is self-contained.

overlap.comparison: Its dilation count gives the corresponding numerical rank exclusion for a saturated same-class lattice polytope. It does not state the lifted singleton exhaustion and affine-height depth conclusion.

Its proof also uses distinct triangulation midpoints, while its main assertion assumes weighted positive-dimensional fibers and a weight-spread hypothesis. The reviewed claim concerns a complete measured counting equality case.

readability: The phrase 'N bases of S belong to one parity class' is read as the count of that full class, matching the exact statement's classification and source locator.
review_method: Independent cold read of the frozen proof, then original-source and accepted-predecessor comparison.
summary: The triangulation count forces a primitive consecutive chain at equality, and singleton heights give affine pairing and the stated counting depth.
